solution:
from typing import List, Tuple


def lz77_encode(text: str, window: int, max_len: int) -> List[Tuple[int, int, str]]:
    """ Compress ASCII text with greedy LZ77 and return the tokens (offset, length, next).
    Start at position i = 0. A match at start j (with j >= 0 and i - window <= j < i)
    has length L: the largest L with text[j + t] == text[i + t] for every t < L, also
    limited by L <= max_len and i + L < len(text), because every token ends with the
    literal character next = text[i + L]. A match may run past i (overlap). Take the
    longest L over all allowed j; if L >= 1 emit (i - j, L, text[i + L]) using the
    nearest such j (smallest offset), otherwise emit (0, 0, text[i]). Then advance i
    by L + 1 and repeat until i reaches len(text). If window < 1 or max_len < 1 no
    match is allowed and every token is a literal. An empty text gives [].
    >>> lz77_encode('abababc', 4, 10)
    [(0, 0, 'a'), (0, 0, 'b'), (2, 4, 'c')]
    >>> lz77_encode('aaaa', 8, 2)
    [(0, 0, 'a'), (1, 2, 'a')]
    """

    tokens = []
    n = len(text)
    i = 0
    while i < n:
        best_len, best_off = 0, 0
        if window >= 1 and max_len >= 1:
            for j in range(i - 1, max(0, i - window) - 1, -1):
                length = 0
                while (length < max_len and i + length < n - 1
                       and text[j + length] == text[i + length]):
                    length += 1
                if length > best_len:
                    best_len, best_off = length, i - j
        tokens.append((best_off, best_len, text[i + best_len]))
        i += best_len + 1
    return tokens
